findings.reason: splitting into two nodes changes dispatch granularity and lets each mechanism land and be reviewed independently, which the single section-level status does not allow.
findings.text: §10 fixes two distinct mechanisms in one node: (1) promotion merges dimension_dispositions/responses/response_events from staging copies into the committed record (promotion.py), and (2) plan_review.record_response writes to the committed record and commits it through _commit_state_write (plan_review.py/review.py); the section carries one data-status and one done-when paragraph over both, so neither half can be closed on its own verdict — the same shape §8 was split on.

response_events.reason: both halves write through the committed-record writer in reckon/crew/review.py, so two nodes would run in sequence on the same file; the done-when already gives each half its own test and its own failing control, so neither half's verdict is hidden inside the other
